page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 6 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 48.0 GB of system memory and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. No GPU accelerators are included in this hardware profile.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.d1.3xlarge delivers average multi-core processing capabilities alongside weaker single-core performance. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 10% to 25% categories, reflecting the older Intel CPU architecture. However, multi-threaded tasks such as bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Geekbench ray tracing achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance for both small and large block reads and writes, though Passmark memory scores are relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.3xlarge offers high storage density per resource unit, making it a practical option for workloads requiring massive local capacity without demanding cutting-edge compute performance. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on slower HDD storage and older CPU architecture, which limits its suitability for high-speed transactional databases. It is best suited for cold data storage, large-scale log processing, data archiving, and distributed file systems where storage volume is prioritized over high IOPS.
